items.name: reflex-dev/xy
items.brief: Fourth day on the list and the only entry today confirmed by three unrelated collectors — npm downloads, GitHub stars and HackerNews. Downloads are up 41% week over week against 4.4% star growth, and 65 open issues on 1,296 stars is a high ratio: people are running it in anger rather than admiring it. The watcher count sits at 3, which is the one discordant note — almost nobody has committed to following the project despite using it.
items.description: Ultra-fast and customizable Python charts

items.name: mokshablr/gander
items.brief: 207 HackerNews points and 75 comments against 287 stars and 4 forks. Attention running well ahead of adoption: a lot of people read about it, very few took it home. Stars grew 7.4% and forks 9.1% overnight, so the gap is closing slowly rather than not at all. It has already left the front page, which makes the next two days the test.
items.description: Take a gander at any file. Offline, zero-permission Android viewer for PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, photos, video, audio, Markdown and code.

items.name: createcentercv.org
items.brief: Movement across three independent readings — Majestic, OpenPageRank and Tranco — but all of it small: rank up 5%, subnets up 1.4%. The value here is the agreement rather than the size. Three unrelated crawls noticing the same modest climb is a different claim from one crawl noticing a big one.
items.description: Because Only Together We Can Build a World Where All Youth Are Safe, Strong & Valued Read More Who We Are Partnering to build a world where all children are lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur. Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipisicing elit, sed do eiusmod tempor incididunt ut labo

items.name: wikif1.org
items.brief: An F1 wiki with 1.5% rank movement and 1% subnet growth. Genuinely marginal — it clears the corroboration bar because two independent sources both registered the same small climb. Listed for honesty about what today's threshold admits.
items.description: Independent F1 coverage — news, driver standings, race schedule, results and stats for the 2026 Formula 1 season.

items.name: playscrabble.com
items.brief: Same shape as createcentercv: three sources, all agreeing, none dramatic. Rank up 5.4% with subnets up 2%. A long-established word-game site — this is what steady looks like, and it is here to show that the corroboration rule fires on ordinary movement too, not only on spikes.
items.description: Play Scrabble online for free on PlayScrabble.com with thousands of members from around the world. Have fun playing with friends or challenging the computer!

items.name: mondomedia.com
items.brief: Referring IPs up 29% and subnets up 28% — one new link per network, which is the healthy shape. Rank change of 35% on an established media domain. The near-identical IP and subnet growth is what genuine link acquisition looks like and is the clearest contrast on this page with the Omsk entry.
items.description: Short, viral and deadly funny! Mondo is where frowns and sadness go to die, and animated series sip champagne and eat the finest mermaid sushi.

items.name: pui68cenil.com
items.brief: Tranco up 9.6% on a domain whose name is meaningless. A pronounceable-word-plus-digits pattern on a .com with no other signal is the shape spam takes, and the gate has not caught it because nothing about it triggers the existing rules. Flagged here rather than quietly published as a discovery.
items.description: Pui68 : Masuk ke permainan online dengan fitur canggih. Agen yang menawarkan akses permainan yang mudah untuk di akses setiap orang.

items.name: drumih/turbo-fieldfare
items.brief: Third day climbing and the shape got better, not worse: stars up 25% to 3,848 while forks rose 33% and open issues 58%. Forks and issues both outpacing stars means people are running the code and hitting real edges, not bookmarking it. HackerNews has gone quiet — comments up only 1.5%, off the front page — so this is now growing on its own without a thread pushing it, which is the transition most launches never make.
items.description: Gemma 4 26B-A4B inference in ~2 GB of RAM on any M-series MacBook

items.name: DramaWave - Dramas & Reels
items.brief: DramaWave improved its best rank 20% to position 12 while falling 34% in the US, 32% in the UK and 22% in Germany. Charting far better overall while losing every tracked Western market means the gain came from somewhere we do not watch. With 100 million Android installs already, this is a mature short-drama app moving on ad spend, not a discovery.

items.name: FORScan Lite - for Ford, Mazda
items.brief: FORScan Lite's Android installs jumped to 10 million and reviews rose 57% in a day — an enormous move for a paid car-diagnostics tool with only 192 iOS ratings. The install figure is bucketed by Google, so a jump like that is a threshold being crossed rather than a real overnight surge. Worth watching the review count instead: 57% growth there is a genuine number.

items.name: yc-software/qm
items.brief: Stars up 121% and forks up 150% in a day, with open issues up 124% and its HackerNews rank improving sharply. Forks growing faster than stars on a repo this young means people are cloning to modify rather than to watch. Everything about it is early enough that a single day could reverse it, but the fork-to-star ratio is the healthiest in today's set.
items.description: Multiplayer agent harness for work

items.name: Freecash - Get Paid Real Money
items.brief: Freecash improved its best rank 7% while slipping in the UK and US. Paid-reward apps move on marketing budget rather than product quality, so read this as an advertising signal. It has appeared in this set three days running with the same pattern, which makes it a good control: if the system flags it every day, its threshold for apps is probably still a touch loose.

items.name: sqliteai/waste
items.brief: Stars up 74% and forks up 69% while comments more than doubled to 161 against just 9 points. That comment-to-point ratio is still inverted — roughly eighteen comments per point — which means the discussion is an argument, not applause. Yesterday's question was whether the stars were the idea or the fight; two days of doubling suggests the idea is surviving the fight.
items.description: Run the full 2.78-trillion-parameter Kimi K3 model beyond available RAM by streaming activated weights directly from NVMe. A dependency-free, embeddable C inference engine.

items.name: c-faq.com
items.brief: On the HackerNews front page with 47 comments, and its Tranco traffic rank improved 1.1%. This is the C FAQ, a decades-old reference — the traffic bump is a link on a busy day, not growth. Included because two independent sources moved together, which is exactly the case where the rule is right and the answer is still "so what".
items.description: comp.lang.c Frequently Asked Questions

items.name: hillelwayne.com
items.brief: 106 HackerNews comments and a small Tranco improvement. Same shape as maurycyz.com: an individual writer having a good day. The value here is the reverse of a riser — it tells you what developers are arguing about today, which is a content signal rather than a company signal.
items.description: Hillel Wayne

items.name: projectpluto.com
items.brief: 79 comments on the front page with a 0.6% Tranco move. Astronomy software with a long history. The pattern across today's domain set is clear and worth naming: HackerNews plus a tiny traffic bump almost always means one popular post, not a rising business.
items.description: Project Pluto

items.name: seriot.ch
items.brief: HackerNews points up 20% from a base of 4, with one comment. This is noise that cleared the bar because the domain population was quiet. Listed so the set stays honest about what qualified rather than quietly dropping it.
items.description: Nicolas Seriot

items.name: chriscoyier.net
items.brief: 52 comments, front page, 0.6% traffic gain. Chris Coyier is a well-known web developer; this is his personal site. Fourth example of the same shape today, which is a stronger argument for a gate rule about personal blogs than it is about any of these four domains.
items.description: Web craftsman, blogger, author, speaker.

items.name: maurycyz.com
items.brief: HackerNews comments up 156% to 180 with its front-page rank improving 12%. A personal site pulling that much discussion is usually one essay landing rather than a site becoming popular. Worth reading what it published today; not worth tracking the domain.
items.description: Maurycy's blog

items.name: drumih/turbo-fieldfare
items.brief: Grew from 2,196 to 3,038 stars overnight — 36% — with forks up 42%, and it did that after leaving the HackerNews front page. Attention there has flattened to 1% growth while the repo itself keeps climbing, which is the split that matters: the launch is over and the growth did not stop with it. Open issues up 22% says people are running it and hitting real edges, not just bookmarking.
items.description: Gemma 4 26B-A4B inference in ~2 GB of RAM on any M-series MacBook

items.name: marbleos.com
items.brief: HackerNews points up 2,100% to 108 with 65 comments, front page, and nothing else in the system has seen it. This is the earliest shape RiseFinder can detect and also the least proven — one well-received post produces exactly this. Worth a look precisely because it is undecided.
items.description: A workspace with visible files, tools, tasks, and outputs — not buried in chat threads.

items.name: reclip.io
items.brief: Four points, no comments. It clears the bar only because the domain population barely moved today. Nothing to act on.
items.description: Reclip is an AI-powered creator toolkit. Automatically clip the best moments, add voiceovers, remove captions, and download videos — all in one platform.

items.name: reflex-dev/xy
items.brief: The first thing this system has confirmed from three unrelated places at once — npm downloads, GitHub stars, HackerNews. Downloads are up 139% week over week against 9.9% star growth, so it is being installed far faster than it is being admired, and 64 open issues on 1,119 stars means those installs are hitting production. Watch the issue count: at this ratio the maintainer's response time decides whether it keeps the users it is winning.
items.description: Ultra-fast and customizable Python charts

items.name: orangecrumbs.com
items.brief: Three points, no comments, same story as reclip.io. Listed for completeness; a quiet day makes small numbers rank well.
items.description: HN Reader, HN Wikipedia, HN YouTube, and the HN Hall of Fame in one place.

items.name: sqliteai/waste
items.brief: 75 comments against 9 points is an eight-to-one ratio, and that only happens when people are arguing. Stars still more than doubled and forks rose 86%, so the argument is drawing builders rather than repelling them. It is on the front page now, which means tomorrow tells you whether the stars were the idea or the fight.
items.description: Run the full 2.78-trillion-parameter Kimi K3 model beyond available RAM by streaming activated weights directly from NVMe. A dependency-free, embeddable C inference engine.

items.name: sawfwair/mere-run
items.brief: 41 stars, 14 points, 7 comments, and it has already fallen off the front page. It ranks here only because percentile scoring is relative and the population was quiet — a handful of people account for every number on this line. No conviction; listed so the set is honest about what cleared the bar.
items.description: Run local image, text, speech, vision, music, and video workflows, plus model management and a loopback OpenAI-compatible API server. The repo ships the core libraries and the mere.run executable.

items.name: SerhiiKorniienko/bullshit-detector
items.brief: Yesterday this was up 141% on stars and 3,200% on comments; today it is up 5%. The spike is over and it converted very little — 90 stars and 4 forks from 68 comments of discussion. Comments still run level with points, so it remained an argument to the end rather than a tool anyone adopted.
items.description: Agent skills that fact-check the internet: claim-by-claim verification with sources and a 0-10 BS score for any YouTube video, article, tweet, or PDF

items.name: gavamedia/deltafin
items.brief: Forks up 20% and open issues up 40% against 11.9% star growth — the third day running that usage has outpaced attention on this one. Six open issues on 567 stars is still a clean tracker, so the friction is early rather than accumulating. The HackerNews points reading dropped to zero while 87 comments remain, which is more likely a flagged post than a collapse in interest.
items.description: Run full Kimi K3 on a single device. And an OpenAI-compatible API server for local chat and coding agents.

items.name: DramaWave - Dramas & Reels
items.brief: DramaWave improved its best rank 5% while losing ground in Germany, the UK and the US at once — 16% in the US alone. That combination only works if it is charting hard in a market outside the four tracked here. Same short-drama category as DramaBox and the same read: watch the category, not the app.

items.name: Google Gemini
items.brief: Gemini is at rank 3 and moving the opposite way to Claude — up 5% in the UK and 1.8% in Germany, down in Japan and the US. Both apps are trading position market by market rather than one pulling away. With a billion Android installs behind it this is a competitive read, not a discovery, and the value is in watching which of the two takes which market week to week.

items.name: Reelo - Media Hub
items.brief: Reelo holds rank 7 on a paid chart with 10 ratings and 5,000 Android installs. Those numbers do not belong together: a paid chart position that high on that little evidence usually means a thin category rather than a real hit. It slipped in both the UK and US today. Treat as a category artefact until a second source says otherwise.

items.name: LukeTandjung/base-gpui
items.brief: Comments up 66.7% against 4.7% star growth, on a 45-star repo. Everything about this is small enough that a handful of people account for all of it. It scores highly only because percentile ranking is relative — in a quiet population, modest movement ranks well. Worth one more day before treating it as anything.
items.description: A GPUI-native port of Base UI's rich, headless component APIs

items.name: drumih/turbo-fieldfare
items.brief: Forks grew 41.5% in a day against 18.6% star growth — people are copying it to build on roughly twice as fast as they are bookmarking it, which is the healthier of the two ratios. At 2,196 stars with 326 HackerNews comments it is past the point where a single post explains the numbers. It has already left the front page, so the next two days separate a launch spike from a tool that stuck.
items.description: Gemma 4 26B-A4B inference in ~2 GB of RAM on any M-series MacBook

items.name: reflex-dev/xy
items.brief: Forks up 17.9% and open issues up 25.5% against only 8.5% star growth. The same shape as deltafin: usage outpacing attention. At 1,007 stars with 59 open issues this is a project being deployed rather than starred, and the 46 HackerNews comments suggest the discussion is technical rather than promotional.
items.description: Ultra-fast and customizable Python charts

items.name: openai/codex-security
items.brief: Still climbing three days after first appearing: stars up 18.8% and forks up 18.3% in the last twenty-four hours, now at 7,237 and 472. It remains on the HackerNews front page with 197 comments. Sustained growth at this size is the strongest pattern in today's set — most launches decay by day three, and this one has not.
items.description: OpenAI's Codex Security CLI and TypeScript SDK for finding, validating, and fixing security vulnerabilities. npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@openai/codex-security

items.name: alibaba/skill-up
items.brief: Modest movement — 5% star growth on a 296-star repo, with HackerNews points up 66.7% from a base of three. Included because it is corporate-backed rather than independent, which changes what the growth means: an Alibaba repo does not need HackerNews to find users, so early external interest here is a weaker signal than the same numbers on an unknown project.
items.description: An evaluation and evolution tool for Agent Skills.

items.name: gavamedia/deltafin
items.brief: Open issues jumped 300% while forks rose 26.8% and stars 15.2%. Issue counts growing faster than stars means people are running it and hitting problems, not admiring the README. That friction is a better adoption signal than a clean tracker, though it also means the project is about to be tested by how fast the maintainer responds.
items.description: Run full Kimi K3 on a single device. And an OpenAI-compatible API server for local chat and coding agents.

items.name: experientiallabs/world-model-optimizer
items.brief: On the HackerNews front page with points up 40.9% and comments up 22.7% in a day. Stars grew 18.6% but the watcher count sits at 1 against 255 stars — almost nobody has committed to following it. That gap is the thing to watch: front-page attention with no followers usually evaporates within the week.
items.description: Build continually improving models on your agent traces by distilling frontier open models

items.name: mishushakov/desktui
items.brief: Appears in today's corroborated set on both GitHub and HackerNews. Early-stage terminal UI work, and like base-gpui the absolute numbers are small enough that the percentages overstate the case. Listed for completeness rather than conviction.
items.description: A remote desktop for your terminal

items.name: FrigadeHQ/yap
items.brief: Modest and clean — stars up 8% to 290, forks up 16%, 104 HackerNews points with 43 comments. Nothing here is dramatic, which is why it is worth noting: the numbers are in proportion to each other rather than one spiking alone.
items.description: Free, open source voice dictation for macOS. On-device transcription with Apple's Speech framework. No cloud, no API keys, no account.

items.name: SerhiiKorniienko/bullshit-detector
items.brief: Comments jumped 3,200% to 66 and points 178% to 62 — a one-to-one comment-to-point ratio, which almost always means argument rather than approval. Open issues rose 800% from a tiny base while stars grew 28%. It has already fallen off the front page, so the next two days decide whether the attention converts into anything.
items.description: Agent skills that fact-check the internet: claim-by-claim verification with sources and a 0-10 BS score for any YouTube video, article, tweet, or PDF

items.name: wassgha/rescript
items.brief: Forks up 11% and open issues up 40% against 16% star growth, with 43 forks on 384 stars. That ratio is unusually high — better than one fork per nine stars — and suggests a tool people modify for their own use rather than adopt as-is.
items.description: 🎬 Open source, transcript-based video/audio editor that lives in the browser.

items.name: openai/codex-security
items.brief: Forks up 70% and open issues up 84% against 47% star growth, reaching 6,090 stars and 399 forks. Issues climbing faster than stars is the signature of a repository people are running rather than reading, and at this size that means real deployments hitting real edges. On the HackerNews front page with 197 comments, which explains the arrival but not the fork ratio — that part is adoption.
items.description: OpenAI's Codex Security CLI and TypeScript SDK for finding, validating, and fixing security vulnerabilities. npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@openai/codex-security

items.name: gavamedia/deltafin
items.brief: Forks up 63% against 42% star growth, on the HackerNews front page with 87 comments. A fork-to-star ratio that high on a 429-star project means people are cloning to modify, not to bookmark. Open issues sitting at 1 says nobody has hit a wall yet, which is either a clean codebase or too early to tell.
items.description: Run full Kimi K3 on a single device. And an OpenAI-compatible API server for local chat and coding agents.

items.name: twalichiewicz/HNewhere
items.brief: 419 HackerNews points with comments up 22%, but only 192 stars and 7 forks. Attention running far ahead of adoption: a lot of people found it interesting and very few took it home. It has left the front page, so this is close to its peak unless the star count starts closing the gap.
items.description: A lightweight userscript that adds Hacker News discussions to any previously submitted article.

items.name: Freecash - Get Paid Real Money
items.brief: Freecash improved its best rank 4.9% to position 10 while losing ground in Germany, the UK and the US simultaneously. That combination means it charted hard somewhere outside the four markets tracked here. Paid-reward apps move on advertising budget, so read the climb as media spend rather than product adoption.

items.name: Google Gemini
items.brief: Gemini improved its best rank 1.9% to position 4, up in Germany and the UK, down in Japan. Mirror image of Claude on the same day, which is the pattern worth watching: the two are trading position market by market rather than one pulling away from the other.

items.name: Parchment: Agenda & Daily Note
items.brief: Parchment improved its best paid-chart rank 12% while falling in all three tracked paid markets, on just 124 ratings and a million Android installs. The rating count is far too small for the install figure, which usually means the Android and iOS audiences are very different sizes — worth checking before treating either number as the whole picture.

items.name: Claude by Anthropic
items.brief: Claude held the number one position across its tracked storefronts, gaining 3.6% in the UK while slipping slightly in Japan and the US. At 50 million Android installs and 215,000 ratings this is a competitive read rather than a discovery — the value is in which market moves which way, week to week.
